entry.title: Add-on: isi audio kata juga, bukan cuma kalimat
entry.content:
Add-on: isi audio kata juga, bukan cuma kalimat

Tiap target sekarang boleh punya dua pasangan: sentence -> audio seperti
dulu, dan word -> word_audio yang baru. Kata dibacakan dari field
bacaannya lebih dulu -- 引数 keluar ひきすう -- karena tidak ada mesin yang
menebak itu dari kanjinya. Untuk JPMN dipakai WordReadingHiragana, bukan
WordReading: yang terakhir berbentuk 単語[たんご], dan clean() membuang
kurungnya sehingga yang tersisa justru kanjinya.

Kata dikirim dengan nada=0. Bridge sekarang menghormatinya di /tts; kata
tunggal tidak punya adegan untuk dinadai, dan di Irodori satu panggilan
model bahasa per kata itu mahal untuk hasil yang dibuang. Bridge lama
mengabaikan parameternya, jadi add-on baru aman bertemu bridge lama.

Dua bug yang muncul persis saat dua pasangan berbagi note type:

- pending() mencari target dengan next() per note type, jadi pasangan
  kedua selalu menyaring dengan field audio pasangan pertama. Tiap entri
  hasil resolved() sekarang membawa nama dan ordinalnya sendiri.

- Note yang butuh dua kolom dimuat dua kali sebagai dua objek terpisah,
  dan yang kedua dimuat sebelum yang pertama disimpan -- update_notes
  menulis balik kolom kalimat yang masih kosong. Pekerjaan sekarang
  dikelompokkan per note: satu objek, semua kolomnya.

run_bulk mencatat ke log di tiap cabang. "Tidak jalan" tanpa log berarti
menebak apakah yang kosong itu pencariannya, koneksinya, atau kartunya.

Config bawaan dapat Retro (Kiku) dan pasangan word di semua note type.
Anki menyimpan config pengguna terpisah, jadi target baru tidak masuk
sendiri ke pemasangan lama -- config.md menjelaskan Restore Defaults.

Diuji dengan koleksi Anki asli yang terpisah: sintaks "note:Retro (Kiku)"
ketemu, 3 note x 2 kolom terisi lewat bridge, hash nama berkas dihitung
ulang dan membuktikan kata dibaca dari bacaannya, jalur SentenceFurigana
menghasilkan kalimat tanpa ruby.

entry.title: Read mined sentences with Fish Audio, hosted and without a card
entry.content:
Read mined sentences with Fish Audio, hosted and without a card

A third engine beside VOICEVOX and Irodori. It runs on Fish Audio's servers, so
it needs no graphics card and nothing to install -- which is the wall Irodori
put in front of anyone without an NVIDIA card, and a 6 GB one at that.

A voice here is a model id from their public library rather than a folder of
recordings. That removes the problem that took the longest to see: every failed
clone in testing failed because of its source material, not its settings, and
material is exactly what an id spares you. Add voice takes the page link or the
bare id and fetches the name from the catalogue, so a list of thirty-two hex
characters never has to be read by a human.

Measured against the chain it replaces: 1.2-3.0 s for a new sentence where
Irodori plus the scene-tone call took about seventeen.

The Reading tab now swaps its lower half to suit the engine instead of showing
every engine's settings at once. Server and Download engine mean nothing for an
engine running on somebody else's machine, and a row that cannot work should not
be sitting there inviting a click. VOICEVOX shows neither.

Three things the tests hold in place:

The key never leaves this machine's config. It is empty in the source and lives
only in phicorvi_config.json, which is ignored; /status reports has_key and never
the key, because that port answers anything on the machine.

The mined sentence is never altered. Scene tone inserts emoji that only Irodori
reads as delivery instructions -- let it run for Fish and they would be spoken as
words, so it stays off and the sentence goes out exactly as mined.

A failure still yields a card. Fish falling over drops to VOICEVOX, uncached and
declared in X-Engine. That is what makes a free tier ending one day an
inconvenience rather than a broken field in Anki.

Also fixed: Fish returns WAV declaring a placeholder length of 0xFFFFFF.., so
anything trusting the header reads a three-second clip as thirteen hours; the
header is rewritten before the audio goes anywhere. And minsize rises 520 -> 560,
measured: at 520 every tab overflowed by 54 px and the rightmost buttons sat
outside the window with no way to reach them. That number was always a promise
the layout could not keep.

entry.title: Say that the exe and the add-on are not alternatives
entry.content:
Say that the exe and the add-on are not alternatives

A release carries two files and the README described only one of them,
so the obvious reading is that they are two ways to install the same
thing. They are not: the add-on sends a sentence to localhost:8772 and
waits, which does nothing with the app closed. Yomitan never needs the
add-on at all.

Both Irodori guides now say the add-on is a prerequisite up front, next
to the graphics card. Download engine puts the engine inside the add-on
folder, so someone who skipped it gets the fallback location without
ever being told there was a choice.

entry.title: Show the install progress that was already being computed
entry.content:
Show the install progress that was already being computed

The installer reported bytes for uv, the server source and the model
weights, and a single static line for `uv sync` -- which is three
quarters of the download and nearly all of the time. Its stderr was read
after the process ended, so the longest phase of the install gave no
sign of life at all. That is the same complaint answered for server
startup, left standing somewhere ten times longer.

It now reads uv's output as it arrives and counts finished packages
against announced ones. The denominator is the union of both: uv
announces lazily, so a package that downloads fast enough appears only
as "Downloaded", and counting against announcements alone produced
"6/4" and a bar that walked backwards. A bar that walks backwards reads
as failure.

The fraction was already there -- `lapor` took it, `_rentang` mapped
each step onto a slice of the whole -- and the window threw it away.
There is now a progress bar to receive it, hidden until an install runs.
The slices are rebalanced to match the bytes: the weights had 36% of the
bar for a quarter of the download, and `uv sync` had a single point.

entry.title: Say what the download actually costs
entry.content:
Say what the download actually costs

Both guides quoted 11 GB, which is the installer's disk check, not the
size. Measured: ~5 GB downloaded, ~6 GB used, and the model is 1.3 GB of
that -- the other 7 GB is PyTorch and CUDA, the entry cost of any neural
TTS. Quoting the safety margin as the price made it sound twice as
expensive as it is.

entry.title: A guide for Irodori, in both languages
entry.content:
A guide for Irodori, in both languages

The release notes say what the feature is. Neither says what makes it
work, which is not the settings: it is whether the reference recording is
one person talking, without music behind them, for ten clean seconds.
Every failed clone in testing came from the material, and none came from
a setting.

So both guides lead with the requirements and the download size, before
the first button is pressed, rather than after eleven gigabytes.

entry.title: Read mined sentences with Irodori, and with the scene's tone
entry.content:
Read mined sentences with Irodori, and with the scene's tone

VOICEVOX reads from a dictionary, which is why it stays the default: a rare
word is spoken correctly rather than guessed at. What it cannot do is sound
like anyone in particular, or like the scene the sentence came from.

Irodori copies a voice from one recording and reads at the same time, so there
is no conversion stage after it. A voice is now a folder of recordings under
user_files/irodori/voice_model/, named after the character; the server is told
their paths directly, because it does not scan subfolders itself. Only the
first eight seconds are used, so the first file in a folder decides the voice.

Scene tone marks each sentence with the emoji Irodori reads as delivery. The
reply is only used when removing the emoji gives the sentence back character
for character -- a model that paraphrases or "corrects" a rare kanji fails that
check and is discarded. In a vocabulary tool, a card that reads back something
other than what was mined is worse than a card read flatly. It runs on whole
sentences only: a Yomitan word lookup has no scene to have a tone, and paying a
model call for one bought about ten seconds of queue for nothing.

The engine installs itself on request, into the add-on folder rather than
beside the exe -- that is the folder every user has, and user_files survives
add-on upgrades. uv brings its own Python, so the machine needs neither Python
nor git. The add-on tells PhiCorvi where it lives over the bridge it already
uses, which beats guessing at four platform layouts and two possible folder
names.

Settings move from one long scrolling panel into tabs. Everything that changes
the sound is in the cache key, and /tts now says which engine actually spoke,
because the fallback to VOICEVOX sounds like success.

An earlier attempt lent the voice a different way: send every finished sentence
through a voice-conversion model. It worked, and cost about twelve seconds a
sentence for a second local service and one more generation of loss. Irodori
does the same thing from a recording, in one stage, so that path is not part of
this.

entry.title: Follow the app's voice, make the switch reachable, make the buttons h…
entry.content:
Follow the app's voice, make the switch reachable, make the buttons hittable

Three faults, all of them the same shape: something the app appeared to control
was actually decided elsewhere.

The voice. The add-on carried its own speaker id, so every mined sentence came
out in the whisper voice no matter what the app showed -- two places holding
one setting, and the invisible one winning. It now sends no voice at all unless
somebody pins one, and the bridge answers with X-Speaker so the filename still
tells two voices apart. Reordering in the app is what picks the voice again.

The switch. Turning off sentence audio meant editing JSON, so mining from video
kept synthesising a second reading of audio that arrived with the card. It is a
checkable item in a Tools submenu now, next to the bulk fill.

The buttons. The clipboard toggle was a checkbox in a corner and "speak any
text" was a text link in a section header -- 41px targets now, in their own
card, which is where the two things people use while reading belong.

entry.title: Tell people when a new version is out
entry.content:
Tell people when a new version is out

Neither piece could announce itself: the app had no version at all, and Anki
only auto-updates add-ons it installed from AnkiWeb, so a file-installed one
leaves checking GitHub by hand as the only way to find out.

Both now read the /releases/latest redirect, not the API. The API allows 60
unauthenticated calls an hour counted per IP, and behind a shared address --
a phone network, a campus, a CDN -- that budget is regularly spent by
strangers before the app ever asks; this repo's own quota was exhausted while
testing. The redirect has no such limit and needs no body.

The app asks once at startup, the add-on once a day, and both stay silent
unless there is genuinely something newer. check_updates turns it off.

entry.title: Read the sentence from the furigana field when the plain one is empty
entry.content:
Read the sentence from the furigana field when the plain one is empty

Yomitan's {sentence} gets switched off when a source hands it messy text, but
the furigana version stays mapped -- the sentence is still there, only wrapped
in ruby, which clean() already strips. Taking whichever field is populated
beats asking someone to change a mining setup that works for them.

A target's "sentence" may now be a list, tried in order. On this collection it
recovers eleven notes the plain field alone could not reach.

entry.title: Fill Anki sentence-audio fields from the mined sentence
entry.content:
Fill Anki sentence-audio fields from the mined sentence

A word mined from a novel arrives with its sentence as text and nothing to
listen to; novels have no recorded line to attach. This adds an Anki add-on that
asks PhiCorvi to read the sentence, plus the /tts endpoint it talks to.

The add-on goes through PhiCorvi rather than straight to VOICEVOX so it can get
mp3 back: Anki's Flatpak sandbox has no ffmpeg, and the same sentence as wav is
eleven times the size, all of which syncs.

ffmpeg writes through real files rather than a pipe. Piped mp3 has no Xing
header, because ffmpeg cannot seek back to fill it in -- the audio is intact but
every player reads the wrong duration and some truncate playback.

The note_will_be_added hook swallows its own exceptions. It runs inside
col.add_note(), so anything escaping would abort the add and break mining.
